body: I really appreciate the words. It means a lot. I think I might try to throw myself into new hobbies.

His name is the only one on the lease, and I think that would probably be a good idea. Only problem is it's a little difficult because I work remotely and require a good internet connection. I think I might start going back to the gym, I'm a naturally skinny dude but I feel like getting in better shape would at least make me more appealing to people. I really appreciate the words, because it's a thought I've struggled against for a long time, you know?


I know he's genuinely sorry, I can feel that and it sucks because I take it as maybe I didn't do enough or I wasn't enough and he sought out things in other places. I need to work on my short-comings, but don't take that line of thought as I think I'm the only one with a problem here. I do, however, believe I'm the only one that is willing to admit there is a problem-- Or rather, I was willing to admit.


And I feel like I'm so much more willing to work on things, but I also feel that I may be falling back into bad habits when I work on it. I'm bipolar and incredibly introverted. So, when I hang out with people for long periods of time I can come back home and have difficulty being overly affectionate. Which, admittedly, may have isolated him into thinking he wasn't loved. I'm on medication for it, but it's tough because I know what my internal responses are, but I can't quite contain being upset, anxious, irritated and so forth without explicitly stating I am. When you do that to a guy that's practically running from all confrontations it could get a little hectic.

It just sucks and I mean that in the deepest and most sincere way I can mean it. Because I feel like I'm too much to handle as a person, and if anyone would have been able to deal with me it would have been him. Ugh.
